title: Fourteen Fathoms and One Dark Mark
subtitle: 测量与深度 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 测量与深度（科学与技术·测量与深度）
meta: 主题语境：测量与深度（科学与技术·测量与深度）　|　核心词汇：depth　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 depth 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the surveyor ① measured a depth that no diver in the bay would have entered, and he said the measuring was the whole of the chart. The ② depth, meaning the distance down and not the deep place, ran fourteen fathoms and stayed unmarked; a depth, he said, is the only thing in a bay that is judged by how long it is left unplumbed.

Every ③ depth in that bay had the same dark mark beside it, and the ④ depth at the end, meaning the one they kept for the channel and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever checked twice. A depth, his assistant said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to lower; the surveyor said the lowering is the part that fills fourteen fathoms.

The geologist meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the depth was the whole of the trench, meaning the deep place and not the distance down. The ⑥ depth, meaning the deep place and not any of that, is the only thing in a trench that everybody maps and nobody reaches; depth, she said, is either something you measure or the only word that means both a distance and a deep place. She said the deep place is the part they remember.

By 1956 the ⑦ depth had become a line in a table, and the table had become an argument about the dark mark. The ⑧ depth of the whole thing, the surveyor wrote in July, was one bay and fourteen fathoms of lowering; depth, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to lower. She said the lowering was never mentioned.

The ⑨ depth I remember is the one at the end, which was re-measured in 1971 and is still described as the strangest in the bay. A ⑩ depth, the assistant said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being measured; every depth, she said, is a deep place that has agreed to look like a distance. She said the deep place was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 深度；纵深（指海湾里测得的那一处）
B. n. 深度（指向下那段距离本身，与那处深域相对）
C. 固定搭配：measure a depth 测量一处深度
D. n. 深度（指留给航道用的那一处）
E. n. 深度；深（抽象总称，指一个海湾的全部测深）
F. n. 深度（指测深表上写到、被列出的那一处）
G. n. 深处；深域（指海沟里那片低陷之地）
H. n. 深处（抽象总称，指人人测绘却无人抵达的那片）

items.q: measured a depth that no diver in the bay would have entered
The depth, meaning the distance down and not the deep place
the depth was the whole of the trench
The depth, meaning the deep place
the depth had become a line in a table
The depth of the whole thing
A depth, the assistant said in 1973

answers.why: measure a depth 意为“测量一处深度”，1948 年测量员测了一处海湾里没有一位潜水员肯下去的深度。
depth 意为“深度”，指向下那段距离本身而不是那处深域，它深达十四英寻而没有标记。
depth 意为“深度”，指那个海湾里每一处深度，每一处旁边都有同一个暗色的记号。
depth 意为“深度”，指留给航道用的那一处，是唯一有人复核过两次的。
depth 意为“深处、深域”，指海沟里那片低陷之地，地质学家说这片深域就是那条海沟的全部。
depth 意为“深处”，指人人测绘却无人抵达的那片而不是向下那段距离，是海沟里人人都测绘、却无人抵达的东西。
depth 意为“深度”，指测深表上写到、被列出的那一处，到 1956 年这处深度成了表里的一行。
depth 意为“深度、深”，测量员七月写道，整件事的测深是一个海湾和十四英寻的下探。
depth 意为“深度”，我记得的是末尾那一处，1971 年重测，至今仍被说成海湾里最奇的一处。
depth 为抽象总称，助手 1973 年说，一处深度是唯一会因为被测量而变得更好的东西。
